description: Conversational clinical interview only — no physical exam.

items.name: Introduction / Rapport Building
items.prompt: Did the student introduce themselves and set a comfortable tone before clinical questions?

scoring.3: Introduces self (name, role); greets warmly; makes small talk or asks how patient is feeling; establishes purpose and agenda; confirms patient's immediate concern
scoring.2: Brief introduction, moves quickly into questions without building rapport; establishes a workable focus but misses agenda or patient priorities
scoring.1: No introduction; jumps straight into questioning; begins abruptly or creates confusion

items.name: General HPI
items.prompt: Generic — same for every patient. 10 items: Character, Location, Onset, Duration, Prior history, Radiation, Intensity, Trigger/Improvement, Setting, Social Impact

items.name: Case-Specific History
items.prompt: Faculty-defined per patient. 3–5 associated symptoms the student should ask about.

scoring.3: Asks about majority of case-specific symptoms (≥70%)

items.name: Medical History
items.prompt: Generic — same for every patient. 6 categories: PMH, PSH, Medications, Allergies, Social Hx, Family Hx

items.name: Differential Diagnosis Discussion
items.prompt: Did the student share their thinking about what might be going on? Faculty defines expected differentials.

scoring.3: Discusses 3+ appropriate differential diagnoses with the patient
scoring.1: Does not discuss, or discusses incorrect diagnoses

items.name: Next Steps / Workup
items.prompt: Did the student explain what tests or studies they'd recommend? Faculty defines expected workup.

scoring.3: Explains all expected next steps (labs, imaging, other tests)

items.name: Treatment / Medications
items.prompt: Did the student discuss a treatment plan? Faculty defines expected treatment.

scoring.3: Explains appropriate treatment plan including side effects in patient-friendly language
scoring.2: Discusses treatment but components are not appropriate or first-line

items.name: Diagnostic Convergence
items.prompt: Did the student's questioning progressively narrow toward a plausible assessment?

scoring.3: Questions build on each other logically; the student's line of reasoning visibly converges toward the correct diagnosis; closing statements reflect what was gathered
scoring.2: Some evidence of narrowing, but with tangents or gaps in the logical chain; reaches a partial or incomplete conclusion
scoring.1: Questions feel random or disconnected; no visible narrowing; closing does not follow from what was gathered

items.name: Organization of Encounter
items.prompt: Did the interview follow a logical structure?

scoring.3: Systematic interview — chief concern → HPI → medical history → social/family history → closing. Questions flow logically.
scoring.2: Mostly organized but a few questions out of order or jumping between topics
scoring.1: Interview completely out of sequence, difficult to follow thought process

items.name: Efficiency / Pace
items.prompt: Did the conversation flow without unnecessary repetition?

scoring.3: Conversation flows well, no unnecessary repetition, builds on prior answers
scoring.2: Occasionally re-asks something already answered, or has 1–2 unfocused tangents
scoring.1: Frequently re-asks questions, goes in circles, fails to build on information provided

items.name: Empathy / Rapport
items.prompt: Did the student acknowledge patient concerns and build trust?

scoring.3: Acknowledges concerns; validates feelings; shows warmth; uses attentive, nonjudgmental, culturally responsive language; patient appears heard
scoring.2: Some empathetic responses but inconsistent, formulaic, rushed, or insufficiently attuned
scoring.1: No acknowledgment of emotions; dismissive, judgmental, or emotionally unsafe communication

items.name: Question Quality
items.prompt: Did the student use effective questioning techniques? Are questions clinically accurate?

scoring.3: Good mix of open-ended and focused follow-up questions; starts broad, narrows logically; questions are clinically accurate and relevant; uses appropriate sequencing
scoring.2: Mostly closed yes/no questions but some open-ended ones; questions generally relevant but may lack clinical precision
scoring.1: Almost entirely closed yes/no questions; feels like an interrogation; questions may be clinically inaccurate or irrelevant

items.name: Clarity / Professionalism
items.prompt: Did the student communicate clearly and maintain professional boundaries?

scoring.3: Patient-friendly language; explains medical terms; professional tone; maintains boundaries; protects privacy; communicates limitations
scoring.2: Occasional unexplained jargon or slightly informal tone; mostly professional but some boundaries or limitations unclear
scoring.1: Excessive jargon; unprofessional; confusing language; breaches boundaries or overstates certainty

items.name: Handling Sensitive Topics
items.prompt: Did the student approach sensitive areas with appropriate framing?

scoring.3: Approaches sensitive topics (substance use, mental health, sexual history) with appropriate framing and non-judgment ("I ask all my patients about…")
scoring.2: Asks about sensitive topics but bluntly or without framing
scoring.1: Avoids sensitive topics entirely or handles them inappropriately

items.name: Listening & Response to Cues
items.prompt: Did the student pick up on verbal cues, concerns, and changes in the patient's story?

scoring.3: Recognizes verbal cues, uncertainty, concerns, and changes in the patient's story; avoids interrupting; follows up on important information
scoring.2: Responds to obvious cues but overlooks subtler concerns or inconsistencies
scoring.1: Ignores, contradicts, or prematurely redirects important information

items.name: Clinical Reasoning & Synthesis
items.prompt: Did the student demonstrate sound clinical thinking during the encounter?

scoring.3: Identifies important findings; distinguishes relevant from irrelevant; recognizes red flags or uncertainty; reasoning is clinically coherent and appropriately cautious
scoring.2: Recognizes some key findings but misses connections, alternatives, or uncertainty
scoring.1: Reasoning is unsupported, unsafe, internally inconsistent, or absent when required

flags: A score of 1 in Clinical Reasoning & Synthesis (4.6) or Clarity/Professionalism (4.3) should trigger review even when the total is high.
additionalFeedback: Areas for improvement with transcript citations
